title: Copilot Studio: share workflows with co-owners for collaborative editing
summary: The roadmap description, consumption licensing and existing control operations are supported. The capacity API is valid despite the automatic pre-check; minor corrections should complete the control paths, identify its request properties and qualify changes governed by environment-group policy.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: What carries on when credits run out; controls[1].governs
claims.claim: Environment overage settings let an environment draw on unallocated tenant capacity after its allocation is exhausted.
claims.quote: Selected: after the environment's allocated credits are consumed, it continues to draw from your tenant's unallocated capacity.
claims.fix: Qualify the capacity row's note: 'If a published environment-group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, individual-environment overrides are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy; change and republish the group rule instead.' The cited allocations tutorial documents this exception. The environment setting still determines consumption, but it is not always independently editable.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: What carries on when credits run out

claims.quote: Select Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan to let the environment continue usage through the selected billing plan.

claims.claim: With no overage source enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.

claims.claim: The Copilot node runs on behalf of the Microsoft 365 user selected in its Connection.
claims.quote: In Connection, select or create a connection for the Microsoft 365 account that the node should use. The node runs on behalf of that user and uses that user's mail, files, calendar, and other Microsoft 365 content.

claims.claim: The sharing rules are at Manage > Environments > managed environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing.
claims.quote: In the command bar, Edit Managed Environments. The sharing rules are located in the Manage sharing section.
claims.fix: For the flow-sharing rule discussed in the checklist, extend the existing path to 'Manage > Environments > managed environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing > Let people share solution-aware cloud flows'. The current path reaches the correct section but stops before that control.

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration with EnvironmentName and UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration saves sharing limits.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration

claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing limits cover canvas apps, solution-aware cloud flows and agent flows, and agents in managed environments.
claims.quote: In managed environments, admins can limit how broadly users can share canvas apps, flows, and agents.

claims.claim: The solution-aware cloud-flow sharing rule can stop users sharing those flows.
claims.quote: When not selected: Users can't share their cloud flows or agent flows with any individual or security group.

claims.claim: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share.
claims.quote: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share an app, flow, or agent.

claims.claim: Sharing restrictions do not remove access from users who already had access before the rules were applied.
claims.quote: This restriction doesn't impact any existing users who already have access to the app, flow, or agent before the application of the sharing rules.

claims.claim: Sharing rules can take up to an hour to start being enforced.
claims.quote: After sharing rules are set in the Power Platform admin center, it may take up to an hour for them to start getting enforced.

claims.claim: Capacity management is reached through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Under the Copilot Studio heading, select Manage Copilot Credits or Manage sessions. In the allocation panel, select an environment and specify the number of Copilot Credits to allocate in the Copilot Credits textbox.
claims.fix: Keep the printed route, which reaches the correct panel. Append ' > environment > Copilot Credits' for allocation; in the note give the overage controls in that panel as 'Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant' and 'Capacity overages > Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan'.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes environment Copilot Credit allocations and tenant-capacity-draw rules.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"
claims.fix: Keep the call: the tutorial sets apiBaseUrl to https://api.powerplatform.com and apiVersion to 2024-10-01, so the automatic pre-check is a false alarm. Add to the note: 'The request sets scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements with entitlementId MCSMessages, allocation.quantity, and enforcementRules containing ruleType TenantPool and enabled. This example configures tenant-pool draw, not the pay-as-you-go overage option.'

claims.claim: Managing credit allocations requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or equivalent licensing-and-capacity permissions.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.
